content:
Although the focus this week has been grabbed by the iOS 27 public beta, Apple has also released a new public beta firmware for AirPods at the same time. This update finally brings a long-awaited feature to supported AirPods models: custom EQ.

AirPods Public Beta Details

The firmware version for this AirPods public beta is 9.0.314, with build number 9A314b. The following AirPods models are eligible for the update:

  • AirPods Pro 3
  • AirPods Pro 2 (Lightning and USB-C versions)
  • AirPods 4
  • AirPods 4 with Active Noise Cancellation
  • AirPods Max 2

You can enrol in the AirPods public beta programme within the "Settings" app on your iPhone. When AirPods are connected, you will see a toggle in the "Settings" app to enable the beta firmware. Thereafter, as long as your AirPods are in their charging case and within range of the paired iPhone, the beta will download and install automatically.

  • Open the "Settings" app
  • Tap "Bluetooth"
  • Tap the (i) icon next to your AirPods
  • Scroll down and enable "AirPods Beta Updates"

Custom EQ Lands on AirPods

After installing the AirPods public beta, a long-awaited new feature will appear in the "Settings" app: custom EQ.

Thanks to the new custom EQ controls, you can now fine-tune the sound of your AirPods in greater detail. Within the "Settings" app, you can adjust the AirPods' bass, mids and treble.

Apple explains: "AirPods are designed and engineered by Apple to faithfully reproduce the sound of music, TV shows, movies and calls. If you prefer a different sound signature, you can also customise how your AirPods perform when playing any audio."

While adjusting the custom EQ, you can play songs from Apple Music directly within the "Settings" app to hear the effects of your adjustments in real time.

This is by no means the most professional equaliser feature out there — it's just a basic three-band system. However, for AirPods users, this is a feature that has been a long time coming, and Apple has finally relented and given it to everyone — even though most people will probably stick with the default settings.

You can find the new custom EQ feature under the "Audio & Routing" menu in your AirPods settings within the "Settings" app. This feature is available on all AirPods equipped with the H2 chip, including AirPods Pro 2, AirPods Pro 3, AirPods 4 and AirPods Max 2.

Other New Features iOS 27 Brings to AirPods

Below are the other new features iOS 27 brings to AirPods:

  • "Settings" App Redesign: iOS 27 has redesigned the AirPods interface within the "Settings" app, reorganising the controls into separate menus for Hearing Health, "Find My", Live Translation, and more.
  • Adaptive Audio Slider: A slider has now been added to the "Settings" app, allowing for finer micro-adjustments to Adaptive Audio mode.
  • GymKit: Although GymKit has been around for years, it has always required an Apple Watch to use. As my colleague Zac mentioned, iOS 27 brings the full GymKit experience to the iPhone and AirPods Pro 3.
  • Precision Finding: You can now use the Precision Finding feature via the "Find My" app on your Apple Watch to locate your AirPods Pro 3.
  • Siri AI: When paired with a supported iPhone, AirPods can interact with Siri AI.

Summary

Which new AirPods feature are you most keen to try? Will you give the new custom EQ a go? Feel free to let us know in the comments.
